title: Russian Railways • Enterprise Communicator UX
subtitle: Designing a component-driven interaction system under legacy constraints

facts.label: scope
facts.value: UX/UI restructuring of multi-step operational workflows and introduction of a minimal component system within a legacy application

facts.label: audience
facts.value: Internal employees performing repeatable operational tasks, where speed, accuracy, and predictability are critical

facts.label: role
facts.value: Product Designer responsible for structuring UX behavior, defining reusable components, and introducing a scalable interaction model

facts.label: focus
facts.value: Replacing fragmented UI patterns with a component-driven interaction model

value.text:
The product is an internal enterprise system used for executing structured workflows.

The interface evolved without a governing logic:

items: patterns were duplicated instead of reused
similar actions behaved differently across flows

value.text: A UI kit existed, but without system integrity:
At the same time, the system was constrained by:

items: high cost of breaking existing behavior

value.text: The product functioned, but its UX layer became increasingly inefficient to use and extend.
The system lacked interaction consistency.

items: users reinterpreted UI instead of executing known actions

value.text: In an operational tool, inconsistency becomes an efficiency problem.

Instead of redesigning screens, I introduced a system layer.

1. Identify repeating patterns

2. Abstract them into components

3. Reuse across flows

System Transformation

To replace fragmented UI behavior with a predictable interaction model,

the system was restructured around reusable components.

Shift in Approach

From local UI fixes → to system-level change
From visual consistency → to behavioral consistency

Instead of solving individual screens,
I introduced a shared interaction logic that governs behavior across the system.

Structuring the Flow

From fragmented screens to a structured workflow

The product consisted of multiple disconnected screens.

I restructured them into a clear multi-step flow:
This made the flow predictable and easier to execute.

value.alt: From local UI fixes → to system-level change
value.caption: Together, these decisions transformed fragmented UI into predictable system behavior

value.text:
Component System

Designing a functional system under real constraints

This was not a full design system initiative.

The goal was to introduce the smallest possible system that could work inside a legacy product.

Atoms → Inputs / Buttons / Labels
Molecules → Input groups / Selectors / Status blocks
Organisms → Forms / Action bars / Validation sections
Flows → Multi-step operational tasks

Core Principle

Components define behavior, not just visuals
What was standardized
Why it matters
A component-driven UX layer embedded into a legacy system:
The interface moved from isolated screen decisions to a structured interaction system.
Without structured UX:
→ increasing error rates and operational cost

In enterprise systems:

UX is not about simplicity — it’s about predictability

The goal was not to redesign the product,

but to prevent it from degrading further.
